newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn sets new contract lows on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn sets new contract lows on weather.

text.p: Another set of contract lows were notched early as CBOT corn futures sagged amid nearly ideal crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"It's like a jungle out there with the moisture and the warm weather," a trader said.
The new contract low posted for September was $2.43-3/4 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.46 set Friday.
Selling was broad based with long liquidation in the nearby July adding to losses in that contract, traders said.
The U.S. corn crop was seeded early this year and the good crop weather led to prospects for a bumper crop.

USDA's weekly export inspections report Monday showed U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended June 19 at 27.837 million bushels, within the range of expectations for 25 million to 30 million bushels.

Refco Inc sold one million bushels of December, traders said. Goldenberg Hehmeyer and Continental Grain each sold one million bushels of July and Farmers Commodities Corp sold one half million bushels of July and two million bushels of December, traders said.
At 1111 CDT, corn was 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with July down 5-1/4 at $2.60-1/4.
Traders said Smith Barney sold up to 3.5 million bushels of corn futures.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report gave the market little direction. The CFTC said as of Tuesday non-commercials, including funds, were long corn by about 169.9 million bushels and short by roughly 231.7 million bushels. Commercials were long corn by 710 million bushels and short by 451.4 million.
